verdict.rationale: The only relevant evidence is a community comment listing "code owners" and "protected branches" among GitHub features lost in private repos when downgrading to Free. That confirms GitHub has a code-owners capability, but nothing describes path-based ownership or enforcing required approval from owners. missing for 10: first-party documentation of a CODEOWNERS file mapping paths to owners, documentation of a branch-protection rule requiring code-owner review before merge, clarity on availability for public open-source repos, independent hands-on corroboration.
